statement: triplet_count returns a result r, and r is the number of ordered triples (i,j,k) of indices with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= j < len(b), and 0 <= k < len(c) such that the integer x = a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of 1-bits in its binary representation. Here popcount(0)=0, and triples with equal values but different indices are counted separately.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: triplet_count returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r <= len(a) * len(b) * len(c).
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Let Oa be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(a) for which popcount(a[i]) is odd, and let Ea = len(a) - Oa. Define Ob,Eb,Oc,Ec analogously for b and c. Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = Ea*Eb*Ec + Oa*Ob*Ec + Oa*Eb*Oc + Ea*Ob*Oc, where popcount(x) is the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer x.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: If triplet_count(a,b,c) returns r and triplet_count(a',b,c) returns r', then r = r'. Thus changing any entry of a to another nonnegative value with the same parity of popcount does not change the count.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive. Also a' is a slice with len(a')=len(a), every a'[i] lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive, and popcount(a'[i]) mod 2 = popcount(a[i]) mod 2 for every i with 0 <= i < len(a).

statement: If triplet_count(a,b,c) returns r and triplet_count(a',b',c') returns r', then r = r'. That is, the result depends only on the multisets of values in the three arrays, not on the order of their entries.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive. Also a', b', and c' are reorderings of a, b, and c respectively: len(a')=len(a), len(b')=len(b), len(c')=len(c), and their entries have the same multisets of values as a, b, and c respectively.

statement: For every permutation (p,q,s) of the three sequences (a,b,c), if triplet_count(a,b,c) returns r and triplet_count(p,q,s) returns r', then r = r'. That is, the result is symmetric in the three array arguments.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns r and triplet_count(a2,b,c) returns r2, r2 = 2*r.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive, and len(a) <= 50000. Let a2 be the slice obtained by concatenating a with itself, so len(a2)=2*len(a), a2[i]=a[i] for 0 <= i < len(a), and a2[len(a)+i]=a[i] for 0 <= i < len(a).

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = len(a) * len(b) * len(c).
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive. Also every element of a, every element of b, and every element of c has an even number of 1-bits in its binary representation.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = len(a) * N, where N is the number of ordered pairs (j,k) with 0 <= j < len(b) and 0 <= k < len(c) such that popcount(b[j] XOR c[k]) is even.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive. Also every element of a has an even number of 1-bits in its binary representation.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = 1 if popcount(a[0] XOR b[0] XOR c[0]) is even, and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(a)=len(b)=len(c)=1, and the single element of each array lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every index triple (i,j,k) with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= j < len(b), and 0 <= k < len(c), the integer a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an odd number of 1-bits. Equivalently, r > 0 if and only if at least one such index triple has an even number of 1-bits in its XOR.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a,b,c) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: len(a), len(b), and len(c) are each between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and every element of a, b, and c lies between 0 and 1000000000 inclusive. Also every element of a has an odd number of 1-bits, every element of b has an even number of 1-bits, and every element of c has an even number of 1-bits.
